title: Setup, Part 2: Connect Posit Cloud to GitHub
text:
In Part 1 you made your own repository on GitHub, turned on its website, and opened a working copy in Posit Cloud. Right now the copy only goes one way: from GitHub into Posit Cloud. In this tutorial you make it go both ways, so that the reports and slides you write in Posit Cloud reach GitHub and appear on your website. At the end, your home page shows your name at your own address.
You don’t need any experience with Git. Every step says what to click and what you should see. If something looks different, If something goes wrong lists the usual causes.











GitHub repository
Posit Cloud project




What it is
The shared copy. Public. Keeps the full history.
Your working copy. Where you write R and Quarto.


Your website
Shows what is in its docs/ folder
Changes here are invisible until you push


Direction
pull brings GitHub’s changes down to Posit Cloud
push sends your commits up to GitHub



The routine is always the same: edit → render → commit → push → check your site.










Word
Meaning




Git
The program that records versions of your files. It runs inside Posit Cloud; you click its buttons in the Git tab.


Commit
A saved snapshot of the files you chose, with a short message saying what changed. It stays in Posit Cloud until you push.


Stage
Tick a file’s box to include it in the next commit.


Push
Send your commits from Posit Cloud up to GitHub.


Pull
Bring commits from GitHub down into Posit Cloud (for example, a change you made on github.com).


Personal access token
A long secret code GitHub gives you to use instead of your password when you push. Treat it exactly like a password.


Render
Run Quarto to turn your .qmd files into the web pages in docs/.

title: Setup, Part 2: Connect Posit Cloud to GitHub
text:
Task
Open your cis-3901-projects project in Posit Cloud (space CIS-3901-Fall2026) and keep this page open in another browser tab, next to a tab on GitHub. Do the steps in order; each takes 5 to 10 minutes.

Step 0. Check the packages (2 to 5 minutes)
Rendering the site needs the tidyverse and rmarkdown. In the Console, run:
needed <- c("tidyverse", "rmarkdown")
needed[!needed %in% rownames(installed.packages())]

If it prints character(0), everything is installed: go to Step A.
If it prints a package name, install what’s missing. This takes a few minutes; wait for the > prompt to come back.

install.packages(c("tidyverse", "rmarkdown"))


Step A. Tell Git who you are (5 minutes)
Every commit is signed with a name and an email. Your repository is public, so use GitHub’s private noreply email instead of your real one.

On GitHub: click your profile picture (top right) › Settings › Emails.
Tick Keep my email addresses private. GitHub then shows your noreply address, which looks like 12345678+your-username@users.noreply.github.com. Copy it.
In Posit Cloud, click the Terminal tab (next to Console). Type these two lines, one at a time, pressing Enter after each. Use your own name (a first name and last initial is fine) and the address you copied, both inside the quotes:

git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "12345678+your-username@users.noreply.github.com"

Check: type git config --global --list and press Enter. You should see your user.name and user.email.







TipGood to know



You do this once per Posit Cloud project. If you make another project from a Git repository later, repeat this step there.




Step B. Create your token (10 minutes)
GitHub doesn’t accept your password from Posit Cloud. It accepts a personal access token limited to one repository.

Open the token form: Create my CIS-3901 token. It opens GitHub’s form with the name, description, a 60-day expiration and the right permission already filled in. (Without the link: profile picture › Settings › Developer settings › Personal access tokens › Fine-grained tokens › Generate new token.)
Check or set these fields:

Token name: CIS-3901 Posit Cloud
Expiration: 60 days (past the Dec 4 presentations).
Repository access: choose Only select repositories, then pick cis-3901-projects. The link can’t fill this one in for you.
Permissions › Repository permissions › Contents: Read and write. (Metadata: Read-only is added automatically.) Leave everything else as it is.

Click Generate token. GitHub shows the token, starting with github_pat_, only once. Click the copy icon.
Keep it somewhere safe for the next 10 minutes: a password manager is best. If you lose it, you can always make a new one (see If something goes wrong).







WarningA token is a password



Never paste it into a file in your project, a commit message, a chat, an email, Blackboard or an AI tool.
Anyone with it can change your repository. If you think it leaked: GitHub › Settings › Developer settings › Fine-grained tokens › Delete, then create a new one.




Step C. Your first commit and push (10 minutes)

In the Files pane, open index.qmd. Near the top, replace Your Name with your name (again, first name and last initial is fine). Save the file (Ctrl+S, or Cmd+S on a Mac).
Click the Git tab (top-right pane). index.qmd appears with a blue M (modified).
Tick the Staged box next to index.qmd. If you also see a file ending in .Rproj with a yellow ?, tick it too: it’s your project’s settings file.
Click Commit. A Review Changes window opens. In Commit message, type Add my name to the home page, then click Commit. Read the small report, then click Close.
Click the green Push arrow (↑). Posit Cloud asks two questions:

Username: your GitHub username.
Password: paste your token (not your GitHub password). Nothing appears while you paste; that’s normal. Press Enter.

When the report ends with a line like main -> main, click Close.
On GitHub, reload your repository. Near the top you see your commit message and “now” or “1 minute ago”. Click index.qmd: your name is there.







NoteWhy your website hasn’t changed yet



Your site shows the docs/ folder, and docs/ still holds the old rendered page. Step D renders the site so docs/ has your name too.


Posit Cloud remembers your token for up to 12 hours, in memory only (never in a file). After that, or after the project restarts, it asks again: paste the token again.


Step D. Render and publish (10 minutes)

In the Terminal tab, type quarto render and press Enter. Quarto renders each page and reports Output created: docs/index.html at the end (about 1 minute). Or use the Build tab › Render Website.
In the Git tab you now see many changed files in docs/. Click Commit.
In the Review Changes window, click once in the file list, press Ctrl+A (Cmd+A on a Mac), then click Stage. Every box is ticked.
Message: Render site with my name. Click Commit, then Close, then Push (↑), then Close.
Wait 1 to 2 minutes, then open your site: https://YOUR-USERNAME.github.io/cis-3901-projects/. Reload (Ctrl+Shift+R, or Cmd+Shift+R). Your name is on the home page.



Step E. One habit: pull first (2 minutes)
If you ever change a file on github.com (for example, you fix a typo in README.md there), GitHub has a commit that Posit Cloud doesn’t. Bring it down before you start working: in the Git tab, click the blue Pull arrow (↓).






ImportantYour routine for every work session




Pull (↓).
Edit and save.
Render (quarto render).
Stage and Commit with a clear message.
Push (↑).
Check your site.

Commit small and often. Every commit is a point you can go back to.

title: Setup, Part 2: Connect Posit Cloud to GitHub
text:
Criteria: you’re done when

git config --global --list shows your name and your noreply email.
Your token is limited to cis-3901-projects, has Contents: Read and write, and expires in about 60 days.
GitHub shows your two commits: Add my name to the home page and Render site with my name.
Your site at https://YOUR-USERNAME.github.io/cis-3901-projects/ shows your name.
Your token is not in any file, commit, chat or message.

title: Setup, Part 2: Connect Posit Cloud to GitHub
section: Using GitHub Copilot as a helper (optional)
text:
Using GitHub Copilot as a helper (optional)
GitHub Copilot is GitHub’s AI assistant. Used well, it explains instead of doing: what an error message means, what a Git word means, what a line in a file does. You still click the buttons and make the decisions.
How to get it

Copilot Free comes with every GitHub account, with a monthly limit. Open https://github.com/copilot and start a chat.
Copilot Student (more use, free) requires GitHub Education verification: https://github.com/settings/education/benefits. Approval can take several days, and GitHub has paused new student sign-ups at times in 2026; Copilot Free is enough for this tutorial.
In Posit Cloud (code suggestions as you type): Tools › Global Options › Copilot, tick Enable GitHub Copilot, then sign in with the code it shows. You do this once per project.

Prompts that help

“I’m new to Git. Explain the difference between commit and push in two sentences.”
“I pushed from RStudio and got this message: [paste the message]. What does it mean, and what should I check?”
Open a file on GitHub and ask Copilot: “Explain what _quarto.yml controls in this repository.”







WarningRules




Never share your token with Copilot or any AI tool. Before you paste an error message, check it doesn’t contain a token or your email.
Check what Copilot says against this tutorial. If they disagree, follow the tutorial and ask in office hours.
In graded work, AI use follows that assignment’s AI level (see the AI Use Levels document) and must be logged as it says.

title: Setup, Part 2: Connect Posit Cloud to GitHub
text:
If something goes wrong








What you see
Why
What to do




Authentication failed or Invalid username or token
You typed your GitHub password, or the token was cut off when you copied it.
Push again and paste the whole token (it starts with github_pat_). Still failing: make a new token (Regenerate).


403, Permission denied, or Write access to repository not granted
The token can’t write to this repository.
GitHub › Settings › Developer settings › Fine-grained tokens › your token › Edit: Repository access must include cis-3901-projects; Contents: Read and write. Save, then push again.


Please tell me who you are when you commit
Step A not done in this project.
Do Step A, then commit again.


GH007: Your push would publish a private email address
The commit used your real email while GitHub keeps it private.
Do Step A with the noreply address, then in the Terminal run git commit --amend --reset-author --no-edit and push again.


Push rejected: fetch first or Updates were rejected
GitHub has a commit you don’t have (you edited on github.com).
Click Pull (↓), then Push (↑).


The token stopped working after weeks
It expired.
Fine-grained tokens › your token › Regenerate token, or create a new one as in Step B.


You lost the token
GitHub shows it only once.
Regenerate it, or delete it and create a new one.


Asked for username and token again
Normal: Posit Cloud forgets it after 12 hours or a restart.
Paste the token again.


Commit button does nothing, or nothing to commit
The file isn’t saved, or no box is ticked.
Save (the file name turns black), tick Staged, then Commit.


quarto render says there is no package called ...
A package is missing.
Do Step 0, then render again.


Site still shows Your Name
docs/ wasn’t rendered, staged or pushed; or the browser shows an old copy.
Repeat Step D; reload with Ctrl+Shift+R. On GitHub, the Actions tab shows pages build and deployment finishing.


Site shows 404
Pages is off or set to the wrong folder.
Settings › Pages: Deploy from a branch, main, /docs, Save. Check the address: your username and cis-3901-projects.



Still stuck? Copy the exact message (without any token), take a screenshot, and bring it to office hours or send it through Blackboard. Nothing you do here can break the course template, and GitHub keeps every commit, so mistakes can be undone.

title: Setup, Part 2: Connect Posit Cloud to GitHub
text:
Check yourself (not graded)

You edited index.qmd and pushed, but your site didn’t change. What step was missing?
Why do you use a token instead of your GitHub password when you push from Posit Cloud?
You fixed a typo in README.md on github.com. What do you click in Posit Cloud before you start working?
Does a commit change anything on GitHub by itself?
Where is it safe to keep your token: a text file in your project, a password manager, or a Blackboard post?
Why use your noreply email for commits?



Show the answers


Render (quarto render), then commit and push the changed docs/ files.
GitHub doesn’t accept passwords from Git. A token can be limited to one repository and one permission, and it expires.
Pull (↓).
No: a commit stays in Posit Cloud until you push.
A password manager only.
Your repository is public, and every commit shows its email; noreply keeps your real address private.
